idea.title: Quitting on a tick pulse: char_update reads a freed Descriptor (use-after-free)
idea.text:
## Summary

A player quitting on the same pulse as a tick makes `char_update()` read a freed `Descriptor`. `extract_char`
leaves `ch->desc` pointing at the descriptor and leaves the character in `char_list` until garbage collection, so
when the game loop frees the closed descriptor and a tick runs before the character is collected, `char_update()`
follows the dangling pointer.

- **AddressSanitizer builds** abort with a heap-use-after-free.
- **Normal builds** have undefined behaviour: usually a harmless read of stale memory, occasionally a crash or a
  wrong `is_immortal()` answer.

It needs a quit in the same 250 ms pulse as a tick (ticks are every 30-60 s): rare for people, common for anything
that logs in and out a lot.

Present at `82171fa` (current `main` of both this fork and mattgodbolt/xania; same lines in handler.cpp and
update.cpp).

## How to reproduce

With an ASan build, have several clients create a character and `quit` in a loop. xania-sim's churn trial does this
and crashes it in about a minute (42 quits in 59 s on 82171fa):

```
python -m xania_sim churn --bots 6 --minutes 15
```

```
==95237==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free
READ of size 8
    #0 Descriptor::is_switched() const     src/Descriptor.hpp:163
    #1 Char::get_trust() const             src/Char.cpp:118
    #2 Char::is_immortal() const           src/Char.cpp:113
    #3 char_update()                       src/update.cpp:705
    #4 update_handler(Mud&)                src/update.cpp:882
    #5 MudImpl::game_loop()                src/MudImpl.cpp:332
freed by:
    DescriptorList::reap_closed()          src/DescriptorList.cpp:8
    MudImpl::game_loop()                   src/MudImpl.cpp:327
allocated by:
    DescriptorList::create(...)            src/DescriptorList.cpp:18
    MudImpl::handle_doorman_packet(...)    src/MudImpl.cpp:487
```

## Faulty lines

| Where | Code | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `src/act_comm.cpp:375-379` | `do_quit`: save, `extract_char(ch, true)`, then `d->close()` | starts it |
| `src/handler.cpp:632-635` | `extract_char`: `ch->desc->character(nullptr)` | **the bug**: detaches the descriptor from the character but leaves `ch->desc` pointing at it, and only queues the character in `reapable_chars` instead of removing it from `char_list` |
| `src/MudImpl.cpp:327` | `descriptors().reap_closed()` | frees the closed descriptor, before `update_handler` runs (line 332) |
| `src/update.cpp:882` / `:890` | `char_update()` runs before `collect_all_garbage()` | on a tick pulse, the quitting character is still iterated |
| `src/update.cpp:705` | `ch->is_immortal()` | goes through `get_trust()` to `desc->is_switched()` on the freed descriptor |

## Suggested fix

In `extract_char`, clear the back-pointer too:

```cpp
if (ch->desc) {
    ch->desc->character(nullptr);
    ch->desc = nullptr;
}
```

`do_quit` already reads `d = ch->desc` before calling `extract_char`, so it still closes the right descriptor.
Alternatively (or as well), `char_update` and the other per-tick loops could skip characters already queued in
`reapable_chars`.

## How this was found

It first showed up in [xania-sim](https://github.com/abraidotti/xania-sim)'s regression suite (1 run in 3), during a
scenario that creates a character, quits and logs back in, on an AddressSanitizer build. xania-sim's churn trial
was then written to reproduce it on purpose. It also turns up in the area trial, whose bots quit together at the
end of each level.

why.function:is_switched: innermost frame of a reported backtrace (src/Descriptor.hpp:163)

sim.why: the game still boots and a player can log in
fights and what runs after a kill (autoloot) reach it
logins and quits reach it (lifetime bugs show here)

sections.title: Explorer insights
facts: Bug check `code.lobby-empty-reply` (present, crash): An empty reply at a login prompt crashes debug builds. MudImpl.cpp:711, MudImpl.cpp:740, MudImpl.cpp:854, MudImpl.cpp:890, MudImpl.cpp:915
Bug check `code.lose-level-asymmetry` (present, wrong-behaviour): Losing a level doesn't undo what gaining it gave. update.cpp:480, update.cpp:539
questions: The fix should turn the code check above to `fixed` (it matches the faulty pattern). Does it, and are there other occurrences to fix at the same time?

sections.title: Architecture
facts: `do_quit` is defined at src/act_comm.cpp:342-380 (39 lines): `void do_quit(Char *ch)`
Called from `do_delete` (src/act_comm.cpp:39), `do_deny` (src/act_wiz.cpp:178), `char_update` (src/update.cpp:655); so it also runs without a player typing it

`do_quit` calls `act` (7 definitions), `announce`, `close` (6 definitions), `extract_char`, `format` (8 definitions), `is_npc`, `is_pos_dying`, `is_pos_fighting`, `log_string` (2 definitions), `logger` (2 definitions), `save_char_obj` (2 definitions), `send_line` (2 definitions) and 2 more
`do_quit` reaches persisted or shared state: character lifetimes, player files
`extract_char` is defined at src/handler.cpp:591-636 (46 lines): `void extract_char(Char *ch, bool delete_from_world)`

`extract_char` calls `bug` (2 definitions), `char_from_room`, `char_to_room`, `character` (3 definitions), `die_follower`, `do_return` (2 definitions), `extract_obj` (2 definitions), `get` (2 definitions), `get_room`, `is_npc`, `is_switched` (2 definitions), `logger` (2 definitions) and 3 more
`extract_char` reaches persisted or shared state: object lifetimes
`MudImpl::game_loop` is defined at src/MudImpl.cpp:180-359 (180 lines): `void MudImpl::game_loop()`

`game_loop` calls `accept`, `all` (2 definitions), `bug` (2 definitions), `character` (3 definitions), `clear_output_buffer`, `close` (6 definitions), `descriptors`, `doorman_init`, `doorman_lost`, `handle_doorman_packet`, `handle_signal_shutdown`, `has_buffered_output` and 19 more
`game_loop` reaches persisted or shared state: player files
`update_handler` is defined at src/update.cpp:856-891 (36 lines): `void update_handler(Mud &mud)`
`char_update` is defined at src/update.cpp:655-821 (167 lines): `void char_update()`
`char_update` reaches persisted or shared state: character lifetimes, object lifetimes, player files
`Char::is_immortal` is defined at src/Char.cpp:113-113 (1 lines): `bool Char::is_immortal() const`
`collect_all_garbage` is defined at src/update.cpp:845-848 (4 lines): `void collect_all_garbage()`
`Char::get_trust` is defined at src/Char.cpp:117-128 (12 lines): `int Char::get_trust() const`
`is_switched` is defined at src/Descriptor.hpp:163-163 (1 lines): `[[nodiscard]] bool is_switched() const noexcept`
questions: Is the change local to these functions, or does the fix belong in a shared helper their callers use too?
Does every caller (including automatic ones) still get the behaviour it expects?

sections.title: Design patterns
facts: 155 other functions share the signature `(Char *ch)`; in the same file: `die_follower`, `do_delet`, `do_pose`, `do_qui`, `do_save`, `nuke_pets`, `stop_follower`
In `char_update`: range-for over contents x3 (modern), act() x7 (either)

Across src/: act() 779, std::string_view 625, ArgParser 402, matches()/matches_start() 291, range-for over contents 267, fmt::format 211, sprintf/strcpy/strcat 19, '\0' terminator checks 14, char buffers 10
questions: Which existing idiom does the change follow, and does it leave the function more consistent?
Is there a helper already (in the same file or a header) that does what the change needs?

questions: Are the other places with the same pattern the same bug, and do they belong in this change?
What debt does the change pay down while it's here, and what does it deliberately leave?
Does the change add any (a special case, a duplicated check, a new legacy idiom)?

sections.title: Gameplay
facts: Players reach this with `quit` (from position any up).
`do_quit` also runs on its own from `char_update` (src/update.cpp:655): players who never type the command are affected too (e.g. through an auto setting).

Messages `do_quit` can show: "|cDon't you want to post your note first?|w"; "|RNo way! You are fighting.|w"; "|RYou're not DEAD yet.|w"; "Your duel came to an end as your opponent quit."; "|WYou quit reality for the game.|w"; "|W$n has left reality for the game.|w"; "{} has quit."; "|W### |P{}|W departs, seeking another reality.|w"
Messages `extract_char` can show: "extract_char: null room, ch: {} #{}"

Messages `game_loop` can show: "Running under a debugger"; "Doorman socket not initialized, exiting!"; "Xania is ready to rock via {}."; "Game_loop: select: poll"; "Unable to read signal info - treating as term"; "Caught SIGINT but detected a debugger, trapping instead"; "Unexpected signal {}: ignoring"; "Waiting for doorman..."; "Doorman has connected."; "Unable to accept doorman connection: {}" (+2)

Messages `char_update` can show: "$p goes out."; "$p flickers and goes out."; "$p flickers."; "$n fits violently before decaying in to a pile of dust."; "$n writhes in agony as plague sores erupt from $s skin."; "You writhe in agony from the plague."; "You feel hot and feverish."; "$n shivers and looks very ill."; "$n shivers and suffers."; "You shiver and suffer."
Balance numbers Explorer models from these files: none (the change is behaviour, not balance; Explorer's predictions shouldn't move)
questions: What does a player notice before and after (messages, what they get, what's refused)?
Can a careless or abusive player use the change (or the old behaviour) to their advantage?
Does it change balance for any class, race or level range? If so, which Explorer numbers?

sections.title: Documentation
questions: Does any help entry describe the behaviour being changed, and does it need rewording?
Does the change need a note anywhere else (README, release notes, an issue comment)?
